To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total nondialysable solids of human urine (TNDS) are a mixture of a variety of compounds, including proteins and peptides, nucleic acids, and other compounds, and that the TNDS can be separated into three fractions, one of which (UF-O) can be further separated into four subfractions, each of which contains a mixture of compounds.

the TNDS in human urine can be subfractionated into three primary fractions and that each of the three primary fractions can be separated into subfractions, that the overall chemical compositions of the three primary subfractions are quite different and that each of them contains a large number of different chemical compounds.

the subfractionation procedure described here yields consistent results and is useful for the study of the changes in the composition of the UF-O subfractions in physiological and pathological states.

the isolation and characterization of the nondialyzable substances in human urine.
